shared_interface_decisions.basis: The canonical Civic contracts implement I420System and use an explicit internal module graph; they do not consume IGenesisResident420 at runtime.

Registry publication/discovery is required for deployment and consumer discovery where modules are registry-resolved, but no Civic contract calls ProtocolRegistry during proposal, voting, finalization, queue or execution.
Civic governance does not identify or custody assets. Governed target protocols retain their own canonical asset validation.
420 Governance is the provider of governance authority rather than a consumer of the shared governance-authority interface. The canonical mutation/execution identity is GovernanceTimelock.
No canonical Civic pause or emergency-council authority is defined. Adding one would create a new governance override.
Wallet, Indexer, Status and operator surfaces may present health observations; Civic proposal validity and outcomes do not depend on a health registry.
Canonical voting and execution contain no oracle-derived eligibility, tally or execution condition.
Voting weight is resolved only through the frozen electorate source captured for the proposal; Civic does not independently consume Identity credentials.
Names are presentation/discovery metadata and do not establish proposer, voter or execution authority.
Governance does not settle value. Governed target protocols own settlement-health gates.
Wallets may estimate network fees for Governance transactions, but Civic contracts do not consume a fee-quote authority.
The current Civic core uses direct msg.sender-authorized on-chain transactions and defines no relayed signed-envelope execution path.
Civic tracks proposal/vote lifecycle only and does not own protocol accounting or custody state.
Civic voting authority comes from frozen electorate sources; reusable Wallet/application capabilities must not manufacture governance voting power.
Governance may authorize calls into Treasury/Vault, but Civic has no custody or release authority of its own.
Genesis deployment must deterministically materialize constructor/immutable/state bindings, but current Civic contracts do not consume the shared initialization interface at runtime.
Migration/version provenance is a deployment and governance-release concern. The current Civic contracts expose no runtime migration interface.
No global system-safety bypass, pause or emergency mutation authority is defined for Civic governance; safety changes must use canonical governance/protocol mechanisms.
No off-chain signed governance command or relayed envelope path exists in the canonical Civic core.

Replay resistance is local: proposal IDs include proposer nonces and frozen commitments, ballots are one-time per voter/house, proposal lifecycle is monotonic, and timelock operation IDs are single-use.
Civic proposal validity and vote outcomes do not depend on replaceable external providers.
Governance has constitutional quorum/approval/delay rules rather than asset/protocol risk-limit consumption.
Civic itself does not move assets; target protocols validate their own asset capabilities.
Proposal metadataHash and actionsHash are immutable local commitments. Civic does not consume the shared metadata-commitment interface.
Wallet/client/deployment layers must verify chain identity. The current Civic core has no signed cross-chain command requiring an on-chain ChainContext dependency.

cancellation.decision: Canonical Civic v1 proposals are immutable after creation and have no cancellation path. A new proposal may change future protocol state but may not cancel or rewrite another Civic proposal lifecycle.
cancellation.indexer_semantics: No CivicProposalCancelled event is canonical for v1. Derived consumers must not synthesize cancellation from absent events or from raw timelock legacy operations.

invariants: GovernanceTimelock is the sole Civic execution and governance-mutation authority where SystemAccess applies.
Governance420 remains compatibility-only and cannot create proposals, cast votes, finalize results, queue actions or execute governance.
The shared Genesis interface catalogue does not create runtime dependencies that the Civic contracts do not consume.
No pause, emergency council, capability, Registry, oracle, identity, custody or system-safety dependency may silently become Civic voting or execution authority.
Civic proposals cannot be cancelled in v1 after creation; legacy bootstrap timelock cancellation cannot be used after Civic authority activation.
Replay resistance remains local to proposal IDs, ballots, lifecycle state and timelock operation identity.

follow_up.GOV-AUDIT-2: Harden the canonical lifecycle and authority graph under this frozen dependency/cancellation model.
follow_up.GOV-AUDIT-4: Reconcile Indexer descriptors and lifecycle projections to canonical Civic events; no v1 Civic cancellation event is expected.
follow_up.GOV-AUDIT-6: Implement deterministic deployment/Registry discovery for the Civic suite without promoting ProtocolRegistry to a Civic runtime authority.
